key_insight: SearchOS makes open-domain web search more reliable by turning hidden search progress into explicit shared state and using it to coordinate multiple agents without repeating failed attempts.
engineering_relevance: The framework is useful for building robust information-seeking systems that better manage context, coverage, and search budgets in long-horizon, tool-using LLM workflows.
method: Formulates information seeking as relational schema completion with grounded citations.
Adds Search-Oriented Context Management (SOCM): Frontier Task, Evidence Graph, Coverage Map, and Failure Memory.
Uses pipeline-parallel scheduling plus a middleware harness and reusable skills to intercept stalls and avoid repeated failure patterns.
evidence_signal: According to the abstract, SearchOS ranked first across evaluated single- and multi-agent baselines on WideSearch and GISA.
watch_item: The added orchestration, state tracking, and middleware could increase system complexity and implementation overhead in real deployments.
paper_title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
